name: Conscript Helm
description: A battered iron helm worn by new recruits.

name: Conscript Collar
description: A crude neck guard offering minimal protection.

name: Conscript Chest
description: Padded leather chest armour. Stops the smallest of blows.

name: Iron Ring
description: A plain iron ring. Somehow sharpens the wearer's strikes.

name: Worn Band
description: A scratched metal band. No discernible power remains.

name: Draft Horse
description: A sturdy workhorse. Occasionally charges into the fray with surprising force.

name: Conscript Boots
description: Worn leather boots. Better than bare feet.

name: Conscript Gloves
description: Rough cloth gloves. Barely break-in.

name: Pano's War Helm
description: Legendary questing helm of the lost vanguard Pano. Hums with old power.

name: Pano's Amulet
description: An amulet warm to the touch, part of Pano's questing regalia.

name: Pano's Cuirass
description: The famed breastplate of Pano. Turns aside blows that would fell a lesser fighter.

name: Pano's Signet
description: A signet ring that sharpens the wearer's strikes.

name: Pano's Band
description: The companion band to Pano's signet. Steadies the hand in battle.

name: Pano's Steed
description: Pano's tireless warhorse. Charges with devastating force.

name: Pano's Greaves
description: Greaves that carry the wearer surefooted across any field.

name: Pano's Gauntlets
description: Gauntlets that lend crushing strength to every strike.

name: Oathsteel Helm
description: Forged from oathsteel and the shards of a hundred conscript helms.

name: Weir Kettle Helm
description: Frontier issue. The brim is wide because rain ruins a bowstring faster than an enemy does.

name: Weir Gorget
description: Plate at the throat and nowhere else. The Weir learned which wounds end a watch.

name: Weir Brigandine
description: Riveted from the scrap of three older coats. Every plate in it has already survived something.

name: Causeway Seal Ring
description: Ash-pitted signet of a road warden. The Ashen Causeway still has wardens. They are just not paid.

name: Marchwarden's Band
description: Worn thin at one edge, where a thumb rubbed through forty years of standing still.

name: Weir Courser
description: Bred for the courier roads. Not fast. Tireless, which on the frontier is the same as fast.

name: Weir Marchboots
description: Resoled more times than made. The Weir counts a boot's age in roads, not years.

name: Weir Handguards
description: Cut long at the wrist. A frontier warden reaches into places they cannot see.

name: Relaykeeper's Hood
description: Oiled against frost, hemmed in lamp-black. Worn by the ones who kept the dead lamps burning.

name: Torc of the Quiet Wind
description: Cold iron, warm at the throat. The Watch says it hums a half-beat before a relay fails.

name: Relay Coat
description: Long, grey, unremarkable, which is the point. A courier who is looked at twice is a dead courier.

name: Lamplighter's Seal
description: Proof the bearer may enter a sealed relay. Nine in ten of those relays no longer answer.

name: Vaultkeeper's Band
description: Taken from the Sunken Vaults, which the Watch marked as sealed and the water did not.

name: Relay Charger
description: Trained to run a route with no rider. Several still do, on roads no one has walked in an Age.

name: Frostmere Treads
description: Nailed for ice. Frostmere takes a careless step and keeps it.

name: Lampwright's Grips
description: Scorched across the palms. The lamps of the Watch were never meant to be handled cold.

name: Sable Vein Circlet
description: Archive work. The script around the band is a catalogue number, and the thing catalogued is you.

name: Threnody Collar
description: Worn by a scribe who recorded a Manifestation from close enough to be corrected by it.

name: Mantle of the Sable Vein
description: Black on black, and the inner black is older. The Houses do not explain their dyes.

name: House Sable Seal
description: Opens an archive hall that appears on no map the Houses admit to holding.

name: Vein-Cut Band
description: Split by a hairline fracture that has not widened in two hundred years of being watched.

name: Sable Courser
description: Archive stock. It will not cross running water, and the Houses have never said why.

name: Stair-Worn Boots
description: Taken off the Eternal Stair. The wear is at the toe, not the heel. Whoever wore them was climbing.

name: Archivist's Grips
description: Thin, precise, reinforced at the fingertips. Some things in an archive must be held down.

name: The Cinder-Cuff
description: Wrath-slag, cooled and cuffed. It makes the wearer stronger and angrier in the same motion, and does not distinguish between the two.

name: The Unworn Crown
description: A circlet of a dark metal no living smith can name, made for a head no carving depicts. It has never, in any account, been worn. The Old Guard kept it because they were afraid to be the ones who found out why.

name: The Vanguard's Cold Token
description: Kin to the lost signet: the same unknown script worn nearly smooth, the same cold that does not warm in the hand. Nobody alive can read it. That is the whole of what is known.

name: Colossus-Core Shard
description: Pried from a war-construct that never stood down. It still pulses with the last order it was given, and there is no one left to amend it: hold.

name: Sovereign's Tithe-Mark
description: Granted by the Gauntlet in the name of the founding pact. It marks a fighter as having paid the tithe. What the Sovereign was promised is recorded nowhere a fighter may read.

name: The Sealwright's Stylus
description: The instrument that inscribed null-sigil bindings, the script that holds a thing closed. The Old Guard made few and accounted for every one. This one is not on the ledger.

name: Warrens Lamp-Hood
description: A hood with a lamp bracket sewn at the temple. Both hands stay free, which in a warren is the whole argument.

name: Ratter's Choker
description: Leather, doubled. Goblins go for the throat because it works, so the Weir stopped leaving it bare.

name: Warrens Jack
description: Quilted and short-cut. Long coats catch on everything down there, and everything down there catches back.

name: Tunnel-Warden's Seal
description: Marks the bearer as the one who counts everyone back out. It is not a promotion.

name: Knuckle-Ring of the Weir
description: Worn on the outside of the glove. Frontier smiths call this an ornament and frontier wardens do not.

name: Warrens Pit-Pony
description: Small, foul-tempered, and unbothered by the dark. It has walked out of places its riders did not.

name: Warrens Treads
description: Nailed flat for wet stone. A warren floor is never dry and never once been level.

name: Ratter's Grips
description: Reinforced across the back of the hand. You will be hitting things that are already biting you.

name: Marchwatch Helm
description: Open-faced, because a watch that cannot see is a wall with a man behind it.

name: Watchman's Gorget
description: Plain steel, no device. A marchwatch is not a house and does not want to be mistaken for one.

name: Long Marchwatch Coat
description: Cut to the knee and lined against the wind. Most of the job is weather.

name: Ring of the Standing Watch
description: Given at the end of a first full winter on the line. Most are given posthumously; this one was not.

name: Tally-Ring
description: Notched once a season. A warden with a smooth ring is new; one with a worn ring is rare.

name: Marchwatch Rounder
description: Trained to walk a circuit and stop at every marker without being asked. It knows the route better than the rider.

name: Marchwatch Boots
description: Heavy, and worn through at the heel rather than the toe — the wear pattern of a man who stands.

name: Watch Mitts
description: Split at the fingertips so a bowstring can still be felt. Frostbite is a slower enemy but it is patient.

name: Gravewarden's Hood
description: Waxed against the smell. The Watch is direct about what the job involves.

name: Seal of the Quiet Ground
description: Worn so a warden can be identified if they do not come back up. It has been needed.

name: Gravewarden's Coat
description: Heavy canvas with iron at the forearms, because the thing you are moving sometimes moves back.

name: Binding Band
description: Old sigil-work, worn smooth. It does not hold anything closed any more. The Watch wears it anyway.

name: Warden's Signet
description: Authorises the bearer to open a marked grave. There is no ring that authorises closing one.

name: Gravewarden's Dray
description: Bred to stand still while unpleasant work happens behind it. The rarest quality a horse can have.

name: Marsh Wades
description: Thigh-high and pitch-sealed. The Hollow Marches are where the Watch does most of this.

name: Gravewarden's Gauntlets
description: Iron over leather over iron. Whatever is down there does not get to hold your hand.

name: Salvager's Helm
description: Sealed at the collar with a glass plate. The Vaults are dark before they are deep.

name: Tidewatch Torc
description: Cold in cold water, warm in water that is not. Salvagers do not agree on what the warm kind means.

name: Salvage Harness
description: Rings and line, no plate. Down there weight is not protection, it is a decision.

name: Vault-Seal Ring
description: Old Guard work. It opens one door in the Sunken Vaults and nobody has found which.

name: Barnacle Band
description: Recovered encrusted and left that way. Coast salvagers say a clean ring means a short career.

name: Coastwise Courser
description: Sure-footed on wet shale and entirely unwilling to enter water above the knee. It has its reasons.

name: Shalewalkers
description: Soled in cork and iron. The Drowned Coast is loose all the way down.

name: Salvager's Grips
description: Webbed, tarred, and cut short at the thumb so a knot can still be tied blind.

name: Breaker's Visor
description: Slit-narrow and backed in lead. A Wrought does not aim, which makes it worse, not better.

name: Siege Collar
description: Braced to the shoulders. It exists so the head stays on when the arm stops something heavy.

name: Wroughtbreaker Plate
description: Layered against impact rather than edge. Nothing made by the Old Guard bothers with edges.

name: Sigil-Key Ring
description: Reads a commanding sigil well enough to guess at its order. Guessing is the whole trade.

name: Breaker's Band
description: Cast from the melt of a construct that finally stopped. The Weir keeps the melt and the tally.

name: Siege Destrier
description: Trained to stand under a falling thing. Horses are not built for this and it is taught anyway.

name: Breaker's Sabatons
description: Weighted so a shove does not become a fall. A Wrought's first move is almost always a shove.

name: Wroughtbreaker Gauntlets
description: Built to hold a bar against a moving core until the order stops. Most pairs are used once.

name: Listener's Circlet
description: Thin, and open at the ears by design. The Choir does not cover what it uses.

name: Resonant Stole
description: It hums a half-tone under any sung note. The Choir considers this agreement.

name: Dawnward Vestment
description: Undyed, unadorned, and cut so it hangs still in wind. Movement is noise and noise is interference.

name: Ring of the First Answer
description: Worn by whoever spoke when something answered. The Choir has four. It will not say to what.

name: Attendant's Band
description: Given to those who stand and do not sing. Somebody has to be listening to the listeners.

name: Choir Palfrey
description: Trained to a whisper and unshod, so a procession arrives without announcing itself.

name: Vigil Slippers
description: Soft-soled. The Choir keeps its vigils barefoot where the ground permits and these where it does not.

name: Cantor's Wraps
description: Linen, wound to the second knuckle. A Cantor's hands are for counting time, not for holding.

name: Sovereign's Diadem
description: Worn by whoever currently holds the Dragon bracket. It is returned, always, and never willingly.

name: Collar of the Founding Pact
description: Names the Gauntlet's first tithe in a script the tournament no longer teaches.

name: Regalia Cuirass
description: Ceremonial in cut and emphatically not in construction. The Gauntlet has always been honest about that.

name: Sovereign's Signet
description: Opens the Gauntlet's inner registry. What is written there is the pact's other half.

name: Tithe-Band
description: One notch per climb paid. Nobody has found the ring where the notches run out.

name: Sovereign's Wyrm
description: Not a gift. A loan, from an institution that has never once explained its terms.

name: Regalia Greaves
description: Made to be seen on a stair. The Eternal Stair, specifically, and the Gauntlet knows it.

name: Sovereign's Gauntlets
description: The Gauntlet's namesake, and the only pair the tournament has ever formally issued.

name: The Sundown Ember
description: Rolled at dusk, lit at dusk, and worn behind one ear like a circlet by an archdevil who maintains this is what it is for. The congregation stopped correcting him some centuries ago. It has never gone out, and nobody has ever seen him relight it.

name: The Perpetual Censer
description: A vessel lit some time during the Age of Dawn and never once refilled. There is still some left. There has always been some left. Those who come to kneel do not always remember, afterwards, what they came to ask.

name: Robe of the Long Sabbatical
description: Cut for a being who intended to sit down and has now been sitting down for an Age. Remarkably comfortable. Alarmingly hard to damage. It smells, faintly and permanently, of the room.

name: Signet of Declined Ascendancy
description: He was offered a throne. He read the terms, asked two questions nobody could answer, and went back inside. He says he will look at it again. He has been saying so for four hundred years.

name: Band of the Fourth Reconsideration
description: There were three earlier ones. He is not looking for them. He is fairly certain one of them is in the garden.

name: Extremely Relaxed Hell-Goat
description: It will carry you anywhere at exactly one speed. Attempts to hurry it have never once succeeded and, by every account, have never once been forgiven.

name: Slippers of the Unwalked Path
description: Immaculate. Not a scuff on them. He means to go out. He means to go out most evenings.

name: Mitts of Amiable Menace
description: He shakes hands. It is worse than the alternative and takes considerably longer. He will ask after your family, and he will remember the answer, which is the genuinely frightening part.

description: Reforged with Sovereign Scrap. Made to be seen on a stair. The Eternal Stair, specifically, and the Gauntlet knows it.

name: Sovereign's Gauntlets (Reforged)
description: Reforged with Sovereign Scrap. The Gauntlet's namesake, and the only pair the tournament has ever formally issued.

name: The Sundown Ember (Reforged)
description: Reforged with Stoned Devil Scrap. Rolled at dusk, lit at dusk, and worn behind one ear like a circlet by an archdevil who maintains this is what it is for. The congregation stopped correcting him some centuries ago. It has never gone out, and nobody has ever seen him relight it.

name: The Perpetual Censer (Reforged)
description: Reforged with Stoned Devil Scrap. A vessel lit some time during the Age of Dawn and never once refilled. There is still some left. There has always been some left. Those who come to kneel do not always remember, afterwards, what they came to ask.

name: Robe of the Long Sabbatical (Reforged)
description: Reforged with Stoned Devil Scrap. Cut for a being who intended to sit down and has now been sitting down for an Age. Remarkably comfortable. Alarmingly hard to damage. It smells, faintly and permanently, of the room.

name: Signet of Declined Ascendancy (Reforged)
description: Reforged with Stoned Devil Scrap. He was offered a throne. He read the terms, asked two questions nobody could answer, and went back inside. He says he will look at it again. He has been saying so for four hundred years.

name: Band of the Fourth Reconsideration (Reforged)
description: Reforged with Stoned Devil Scrap. There were three earlier ones. He is not looking for them. He is fairly certain one of them is in the garden.

name: Extremely Relaxed Hell-Goat (Reforged)
description: Reforged with Stoned Devil Tack. It will carry you anywhere at exactly one speed. Attempts to hurry it have never once succeeded and, by every account, have never once been forgiven.

name: Slippers of the Unwalked Path (Reforged)
description: Reforged with Stoned Devil Scrap. Immaculate. Not a scuff on them. He means to go out. He means to go out most evenings.

name: Mitts of Amiable Menace (Reforged)
description: Reforged with Stoned Devil Scrap. He shakes hands. It is worse than the alternative and takes considerably longer. He will ask after your family, and he will remember the answer, which is the genuinely frightening part.
